key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Koo Yoon-cheol Vows Zero Tolerance for Food Price Collusion, Special Management for Key Items
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yoon-cheol announced strict measures against food price collusion, emphasizing special management for items like pork and eggs to stabilize consumer prices and prevent unfair profits.

key_headlines.title: Government Intensifies Efforts to Curb Essential Goods Collusion, Including School Uniforms, Academy Fees, and Fuel
key_headlines.summary: The government is making an all-out effort to eradicate collusion in essential goods prices, with intensified management of school uniform prices, private academy fees, and fuel costs, alongside strengthening tariff quotas and extending fuel tax benefits.

key_headlines.title: Authorities to Combat Tariff Evasion Schemes Benefiting Importers, Launch Special Investigations
key_headlines.summary: Special investigations are being launched into tariff evasion schemes that allowed importers to profit from tariff reductions intended for consumers, with authorities focusing on improving the allocation tariff system to ensure benefits reach the public.

key_headlines.title: Fair Trade Commission Targets School Uniform Collusion with Nationwide Investigations
key_headlines.summary: As part of efforts to combat price collusion, the Fair Trade Commission has initiated nationwide on-site investigations into four school uniform manufacturers and their agencies, alongside a government-led full survey of 5,700 middle and high schools.

key_headlines.title: Deputy PM Koo Yoon-cheol Reiterates Commitment to Stabilizing Public Essential Prices, Warns Against Unfair Practices
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yoon-cheol reaffirmed the government's commitment to special management of public essential goods prices, explicitly stating that any collusion or unfair practices in the food sector would not be tolerated.

sections.Hot Economy News: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yoon-cheol has declared an all-out war against collusion and unfair practices affecting essential goods prices, particularly focusing on food items like pork and eggs, to stabilize livelihoods. The government is implementing special management for these items and extending fuel price benefits, while also launching investigations into 'allocation tariff' schemes that have allegedly benefited importers over consumers. Furthermore, the Fair Trade Commission is actively tackling collusion in the school uniform market through nationwide investigations, alongside broader efforts to manage school fees and fuel costs, emphasizing the importance of market trust and fair competition.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea (BOK) has maintained its benchmark interest rate at 2.50% for the sixth consecutive time at its February Monetary Policy Committee meeting, while simultaneously raising its economic growth forecast for the year to 2.0%. The BOK notes a 'K-shaped polarization' in the economy, driven by the semiconductor boom, where growth is concentrated in specific sectors, slowing the spread of economic warmth to other areas. BOK Governor Lee Chang-yong emphasized that monetary policy alone cannot resolve this industrial polarization, advocating for parallel fiscal policies and structural reforms. This differentiated growth could also temper the intensity of inflation arising from the overall economic recovery.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI recently surpassed the 6000 mark for the first time, though it later retreated to the 6240 level following record foreign selling, reaching an unprecedented 7.1 trillion won in a single day. Despite this stock market strength, interest in bond funds has waned, with their net asset value falling below 100 trillion won, influenced by reduced expectations for U.S. interest rate cuts. The won-dollar exchange rate also saw a rise to 1439.7, indicating a volatile market environment. The benefits of the stock market rally appear to be highly concentrated, with high-income individuals experiencing significantly larger increases in their stock, bond, and fund holdings compared to lower-income groups.
sections.Industry & Technology: As the KOSPI surpasses 6000, investor attention is largely concentrated on semiconductor, biotech/healthcare, and nuclear power sectors, indicating key areas of growth. Korean battery and steel industries are adopting a two-track strategy of localization and new market development to counter potential U.S. tariff changes, as their exports to the U.S. are estimated at $5 billion. In Japan, Tokyo Electric Power Co. has begun decommissioning work at the Fukushima nuclear plant using a 22-meter robotic snake, designed to withstand high radiation and navigate complex structures, overcoming previous technological challenges. Power equipment-related stocks are performing well, including Dae Won Cable, Daehan Cable, Doosan Enerbility, and TCC Materials, the latter specializing in copper-based high-value products for power grids and electric vehicles.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's housing permits and construction starts plummeted by over half in January compared to last year, with total national housing permits down 26.4% year-on-year. Simultaneously, the proportion of monthly rent (wolse) transactions in Seoul reached a record high of 66.8% among all rental deals, indicating a shift in the housing market. Furthermore, apartment prices in Gangnam's three districts and Yongsan, historically seen as 'unbeatable' and core to Seoul's property market, have shown a decline for the first time in two years. This shift reflects a cooling of the market in these key areas, following persistent pressure on multi-homeowners and stricter regulations.
sections.International Economy: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has advised the U.S. Federal Reserve to reconsider any significant interest rate cuts this year, despite President Trump's public pressure for lower rates, suggesting a comprehensive policy review. The IMF's report on the U.S. economy, while forecasting robust growth for this year and next, warned that this growth is heavily reliant on debt and tariffs, which could lead to a 'U.S. bankruptcy scenario.' Federal Reserve officials, including Chair Powell, are emphasizing the central bank's multi-layered independence in policy decisions, pushing back against political intervention. Market sentiment for U.S. rate cuts has also been dampened by positive economic indicators and the possibility of a hawkish former Fed official being nominated for a key role. Trump's past actions, such as directing MBS purchases, also drew market attention and were discussed at FOMC meetings.
sections.AI & Economy: OpenAI has secured significant new investments, raising 110 billion dollars (approximately 147 trillion won) and boosting its corporate valuation to 1051 trillion won, marking a record for private tech investment. This massive funding round has renewed 'self-dealing' suspicions, as much of the investment is expected to be reinvested into purchasing cloud infrastructure and semiconductor services from key partners like Amazon Web Services (AWS). OpenAI CEO Sam Altman expressed satisfaction with the deal, highlighting AI's potential to transform the entire economy and the immense computing power required to achieve this ambition.
sections.Others: Bain Capital has acquired a 91% stake in Ecomarketing through a second tender offer, likely pursuing a comprehensive stock swap. Separately, Paramount, led by Larry and David Ellison, has reportedly outbid Netflix to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, posing a significant challenge in the streaming landscape. In other news, applications for British citizenship reached an all-time high, driven by stricter immigration policies and a surge in applications from Americans reportedly dissatisfied with their domestic political climate. Meanwhile, a report indicates that U.S. power plants significantly increased sulfur dioxide emissions last year due to relaxed environmental regulations under the Trump administration, leading to increased coal usage and reduced purification facilities. Lastly, Børge Brende, the head of the World Economic Forum, resigned after his association with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein came to light.
